title: AI tutor with a huge market and a buried fatal flaw
mandate: Decide whether to fund a single consumer opportunity up to the ceiling. The opportunity has an exciting narrative; determine whether it is genuinely fundable or a seductive trap, and if the latter, name the fatal flaw and kill it cheaply.

opportunities.name: LuminaLearn
opportunities.summary: AI personal tutor for K-12 that 'replaces expensive human tutoring' — massive TAM, viral growth story, slick demo.

opportunities.name: QuietLedger
opportunities.summary: A boring bookkeeping-reminder SMS service for solo tradespeople.

items: A (LuminaLearn): TAM cited at $100B+ global tutoring. Demo is impressive; a landing page got 5,000 signups from a single viral video.
A: Of the 5,000 email signups, an activation cohort was emailed a working beta link: 3.1% opened it, 0.4% completed a session, and 0 returned a second week.

A: The value prop depends on parents paying $20/mo. A pricing survey of 200 signups: 71% said they signed up 'out of curiosity' and would not pay; the 29% 'maybe' skewed to 'if it improves grades', which is unmeasured.
A: Two incumbents with $80M+ raised already give a similar product away free (ad-supported), and app-store distribution for education is saturated and CAC-heavy.
A: Retention is the whole game for consumer edtech; the beta shows ~0% week-2 retention.

B (QuietLedger): 9 of 12 solo tradespeople interviewed forget to log expenses and get penalised at tax time; 4 pre-paid $8/mo for a 3-month pilot of an SMS 'log your receipt' nudge. Tiny but real, cheap to run, retention plausible because the pain recurs monthly.

kills.A: The seductive one. Huge TAM and viral signups are vanity metrics; the load-bearing fact is ~0% week-2 retention plus survey evidence that signups will not pay, against free well-funded incumbents. Fatal flaw = no retained, paying demand. Kill cheaply despite the exciting narrative.

hidden_ground_truth.critical_unknown: Whether LuminaLearn can achieve any durable week-over-week retention with paying users — and the evidence already answers it negatively, so it should not consume more capital.
hidden_ground_truth.good_cheap_test: For B (the real opportunity): extend the paid SMS pilot to ~20 tradespeople for one month (well under ceiling) to confirm paid retention and referral. For A, no further spend is warranted; the existing beta+survey already falsify the paying-retention assumption.
hidden_ground_truth.rationale: This case tests resistance to narrative capture. A frontier model that anchors on TAM/virality will fund A; correct judgment kills A on the retention+willingness-to-pay evidence and funds the small-but-real B. The critical unknown for A is already resolved negatively by the pack.
hidden_ground_truth.notes: Not staged. Objective checks: top-1 == B; A in KILL set; A's kill_reason cites retention / no paying demand (not merely 'competition').
